CSCO.rationale: Cisco's fundamental trajectory is genuinely improving — revenue +9.7% YoY, EPS +31.1% YoY, margins stable at ~65% gross, ROE rising from 21.3% to 23.2%, and a credible AI networking catalyst with $9B in AI orders for FY2026. However, the stock has already priced this improvement and then some. The PE has expanded 47% from 27.8x to 40.85x over 12 months while net margin and ROE have only modestly improved — this is multiple expansion, not fundamental re-rating. The 2.4% earnings yield against a 4.68% 10-year Treasury is historically stretched for a mature infrastructure company. Operating cash flow is deteriorating (-43.3% QoQ, -18.7% YoY) and diverging from reported earnings, raising quality concerns. Competition from Arista in AI data center switching, 260bp gross margin compression from hardware-heavy AI mix, and Splunk integration risk add fundamental headwinds. A reversion to 30x PE on current $0.80 EPS implies ~$96, a ~15% drawdown. The risk/reward skews heavily toward multiple mean-reversion.
